title: SIG Questionnaire Walkthrough - Orion Financial
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Orion Financial through the SIG/CAIQ and the common evidence requests. Key focus areas were SOC 2 scope and bridge docs, SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning, encryption (KMS/BYOK) options, audit log access/retention, and data residency/VPC deployment. Action items and next steps agreed to share SOC 2 Type II report, CAIQ completed answers, infra diagram, and schedule a follow-up technical deep dive for KMS integration.
next_steps: Jamie to send SOC 2 Type II report and bridge letter (by 2026-03-16)
Liam to upload completed CAIQ & CAIQ evidence index (by 2026-03-18)
Schedule follow-up deep dive on KMS/BYOK (week of 2026-03-23)
Share network diagram and private deployment options (VPC)
action_items: Jamie Chen - Send SOC 2 Type II report + bridge letter - due 2026-03-16
Liam Patel - Provide completed CAIQ answers + evidence index link - due 2026-03-18
Jamie Chen - Share Redwood infra diagram and list of subprocessors - due 2026-03-17
Mark Rivera - Provide list of regulatory data residency requirements for pilot - due 2026-03-19
transcript:
00:00:00 - Jamie (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call real quick?
00:00:06 - Sarah Lopez (Orion): Hi this is Sarah, Head of InfoSec.
00:00:09 - Mark Rivera (Orion): Mark here, cloud eng.
00:00:11 - Priya Shah (Procurement): Priya from procurement.
00:00:13 - Liam Patel (Redwood SE): Liam from Redwood, I'll cover the technical bits.
00:00:18 - Jamie: Cool. Agenda today is SIG/CAIQ walkthrough and what evidence you typically need for vendor risk. We'll cover SOC 2, ISO, SSO, KMS options, audit logs, and data residency, and then next steps.
00:00:31 - Sarah: Sounds good, we have the questionnaire in front of us. we'll call out areas we need more detail on.
00:00:36 - Jamie: Great. Starting with SOC 2, Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II coverage for the inference platform and control plane. We can provide the report and a bridge letter for the period of the questionnaire.
00:00:47 - Sarah: Okay can you confirm the scope? Is it just control plane or also data plane for hosted API? We need to know which systems are in scope.
00:00:55 - Liam: Good question. The Type II covers the hosted control plane and the customer metadata services. For customers who choose Redwood Dedicated or Private deployments, those are outside the hosted SOC 2 scope by default — though we provide guidance and optional attestations for Private deployments.
00:01:12 - Sarah: So for Orion pilot we plan to use hosted initially but with EU data residency. Does SOC 2 cover EU-hosted nodes?
00:01:20 - Jamie: The SOC report itself is not region-specific; it covers organizational controls. For data residency we provide region-specific hosting, and we have documentation showing regional controls and subprocessors by region. We'll attach that.
00:01:33 - Mark: On data residency — what's the mechanism? Is data pinned to a region? How do you prevent cross-region failover for PII?
00:01:40 - Liam: We support region pinning on the hosted offering. For stronger guarantees, Dedicated or Private deployments give you stricter residency and network isolation. We also have automated routing policies but you can set policies to avoid cross-region fallback.
00:01:53 - Sarah: OK. Next question in CAIQ is encryption at rest and key management. How do you handle KMS and BYOK?
00:02:00 - Liam: By default we encrypt at rest using cloud provider-managed keys and we enforce TLS 1.2+ in transit. For customers requiring BYOK, our Private offering supports integration with customer KMS and HSM — we support CloudKMS, AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and bring-your-own-HSM patterns. We can provide details on key rotation, key access controls, and split-key designs if needed.
00:02:20 - Sarah: Do you allow Redwood to see plaintext model inputs/outputs for hosted? We need clarity for regulated data.
00:02:27 - Jamie: For hosted, Redwood processes requests in the runtime; we do not persist customer prompts beyond short-term caching for performance unless configured otherwise. We have controls for data deletion on request and retention policy — typical retention for logs is 90 days unless contractual modifications. For regulated workloads, Private deployments are recommended.
00:02:44 - Mark: And for audit logs — can we get raw access or a push to our SIEM?
00:02:49 - Liam: We can stream audit logs to customer endpoints (e.g., S3, Splunk, Event Hub) and provide API access. Logs include request metadata, auth events, and admin actions. Note: payload-level data is redacted by default in audit exports unless customers opt in for full logging in a Private environment.
00:03:09 - Priya: Procurement also has a few items about subcontractors and subprocessors — where do we find that list?
00:03:14 - Jamie: We'll send an up-to-date subprocessors list and a summary of vendor risk assessments. It's part of the security pack link we'll share.
00:03:22 - Sarah: The questionnaire asks about RBAC and SSO. What's supported?
00:03:26 - Liam: We support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. Roles are RBAC-based — admin, developer, auditor, and custom roles. MFA is enforced for Redwood Console logins and can be enforced via customer IdP too.
00:03:39 - Sarah: SCIM sync — do you write back status or just provisioning?
00:03:43 - Liam: SCIM is primarily provisioning and deprovisioning. We emit audit events for SCIM actions.
00:03:49 - Mark: How granular is RBAC? Can we restrict access to specific models or routes?
00:03:54 - Liam: Yes, you can scope API keys and routes by team and model. Policies support least privilege, per-model and per-environment separation.
00:04:03 - Jamie: On the SIG form, there are often questions about pen testing and vuln management — we do quarterly internal scans and annual third-party pen tests. We can provide a high-level report and an executive summary.
00:04:15 - Sarah: Will you provide evidence of remediation for findings?
00:04:19 - Liam: We can provide remediation trackers at a high level. We don't typically share raw exploit proofs, but we share the scope, findings, and remediation closure evidence.
00:04:27 - [00:04:30] Speaker 1 (Orion): slight crosstalk, sorry —
00:04:34 - Jamie: No problem. Next on the CAIQ: incident response and breach notifications. Redwood has an IR plan and notifies customers within contractual SLA; we also maintain an incident page and offer post-incident reports for material incidents.
00:04:47 - Sarah: Notification timeline?
00:04:49 - Liam: We aim for initial notification within 72 hours after triage for incidents meeting the threshold in the contract, but critical incidents are pushed earlier.
00:04:58 - Sarah: Can Orion get push of related logs for forensics?
00:05:02 - Liam: Yes for Dedicated/Private we can provide more forensic access; for hosted we provide exports and support packaged forensic artifacts.
00:05:12 - Mark: There's a question about data deletion and eDiscovery — how do you handle DSARs?
00:05:17 - Jamie: We support customer-initiated data deletion requests and have API and support flows to purge customer data. DSAR operationally is customer-owned; we provide exports and assist per contract.
00:05:27 - Sarah: On the CAIQ there's a field about supply chain security — do you run SBOMs or software bill-of-materials?
00:05:33 - Liam: We maintain SBOMs for our services and can provide summaries for critical components. We also do dependency scanning and SCA.
00:05:41 - Priya: A couple procurement questions: will you sign our standard DPA and do you accept standard SLAs?
00:05:46 - Jamie: We have a standard DPA and enterprise terms. We can review Orion's DPA; some edits may require legal review but typical items like data residency and processor-to-processor clauses are handled.
00:05:58 - Sarah: For the SIG, we'll need a CAIQ with evidence links. what's the typical format you provide?
00:06:04 - Jamie: We usually provide a completed CAIQ spreadsheet with links to evidence hosted in a secure share (eg, read-only Google Drive or signed NDA link). We also include a mapping to SOC 2 controls. Liam will own the evidence index.
00:06:17 - Liam: i'll assemble the CAIQ answers and attach evidence pointers — SOC 2 report, pen test summary, KMS integration doc, SCIM SAML config guides, and the subprocessors list.
00:06:27 - Mark: For KMS, we need to better understand the flow in hosted mode — who controls keys, and what's the seal boundary?
00:06:33 - Liam: In hosted mode keys are provider-managed (e.g., AWS KMS) and Redwood manages the key material. For BYOK in Private, customers inject keys into the runtime, or we integrate with a customer's CloudKMS. We can show architecture diagrams.
00:06:46 - Sarah: Do you offer HSM-backed keys for very sensitive workloads?
00:06:50 - Liam: Yes, Private supports HSM backed keys and we can integrate with external HSMs or cloud HSM offerings. We'll detail supported algorithms and key rotation practices in the doc.
00:07:01 - Jamie: On retention and logging — typical audit log retention is 90 days for hosted; we can negotiate longer retention or streaming to customer's storage for longer retention.
00:07:10 - Sarah: Our policy requires 1 year of admin/audit logs for forensic purposes. Can you provide a retention plan?
00:07:16 - Liam: We can stream all admin and auth logs to your SIEM or S3, which lets you keep them for a year. For payloads we recommend Private if you need full payload retention.
00:07:27 - Priya: procurement question: billing and contract term confidentiality — do you provide SOC 2 attestation for third party auditors?
00:07:33 - Jamie: yes SOC 2 is for auditors; we'll share the report under NDA.
00:07:38 - Sarah: okay great. Now a few CAIQ specific Qs — A12 or AIC controls around change management. How do you track and evidence change control?
00:07:46 - Liam: We use Git-based pipelines, change approvals, documented release notes, and we can provide screenshots or logs showing approvals and deploy artifacts. We also keep a change ticket history for a period per policy.
00:08:00 - Sarah: For vulnerability scanning, frequency and scope?
00:08:03 - Liam: Weekly automated scans and quarterly authenticated scans plus annual third-party assessment covering internet-facing and internal critical components.
00:08:12 - [00:08:15] Speaker 2 (Orion): quick clarifying question on subprocessors — do you use any model providers or third-party model hosts?
00:08:21 - Jamie: We operate our own inference runtime but we do use cloud providers for compute and some telemetry tooling; those are in the subprocessors list. We don't send customer data to third-party model vendors by default.
00:08:33 - Mark: On the subject of backups — where are backups stored and are they encrypted?
00:08:37 - Liam: Backups are encrypted at rest using provider KMS keys and access is restricted. We have retention policies and can provide a backup diagram.
00:08:46 - Sarah: Good. Regarding the evidence — can you provide an index that maps CAIQ question to evidence link?
00:08:52 - Jamie: yes, that's part of the CAIQ evidence index file. We'll provide links to a secure share.
00:08:58 - Priya: Any compliance certificates besides SOC 2? ISO 27001?
00:09:02 - Jamie: Redwood is working towards ISO 27001; we do have partial coverage and can share the roadmap and controls mapping.
00:09:09 - Sarah: Noted. A couple of the SIG items are more technical — we'd like a KMS integration deep dive and a private deployment networking diagram. can we schedule a follow-up?
00:09:18 - Jamie: Yes we'll schedule a technical deep dive. Liam will lead and we can invite cloud eng folks from Orion.
00:09:24 - Mark: Please include expected effort for BYOK integration and any downtime requirements.
00:09:29 - Liam: Sure, we'll surface a migration checklist and the typical timeline — usually a few days to configure and test in staging.
00:09:36 - Sarah: Great. Any questions from Redwood?
00:09:39 - Jamie: No, just to confirm next steps — send SOC 2, CAIQ answers with evidence, infra diagram, and schedule the KMS deep dive.
00:09:47 - Sarah: sounds good.
00:09:49 - [00:09:50] Speaker 1: small cross talk and agreement.
00:09:55 - Jamie: we'll wrap up — thanks all.
